chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) was one day with Ayesha when a man sought permission to enter. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The worst of the clan.' So Ayesha stood up and entered the house, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) gave permission to the man. When he entered, he turned his face towards him with a cheerful expression, speaking with him until he finished and left his presence. Ayesha said: 'O Messenger of Allah! While you were mentioning this man with what you mentioned, then you turned your face to him with cheerfulness?' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said at that: 'Among the worst of the servants of Allah is the one whose company is disliked due to his obscenity.'

key_terms.وَبِشْرُهُ إِلَيْهِ: With a cheerful expression towards him

ai.seo_question: Why did the Prophet greet a man he called 'the worst of the clan' with a cheerful face?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) demonstrates the Shia principle of *Hilm* (forbearance) by greeting a man known for his *Fush* (obscenity/vulgarity) with a cheerful countenance, despite his initial complaint to Aisha. This incident underscores the scholarly distinction between internal dislike of a person's character and the external obligation of maintaining dignified social conduct (*Adab*) with them. It serves as a practical model for Muslims to manage relationships with difficult individuals without compromising their own spiritual composure.
